items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday declined to entertain a challenge to the constitutional validity of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which empowers executive magistrates to issue prohibitory orders to restrict public gatherings in the interest of preventing danger or maintaining peace. The Court, however, has agreed to examine various prohibitory orders issued under the said provision in connection with the recent Delhi protests. The Court will also examine a challenge to the validity of Section 172 of the BNSS, which requires persons to comply with lawful directions issued by police officers and gives the police the power to detain those who defy such directions and obstruct police duties. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi yesterday sought the response from the Central government, the Delhi government, the Delhi Commissioner of Police and other authorities on a plea challenging this provision. CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi During the hearing, Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal , representing a petitioner, had questioned the exercise of powers under the BNSS provisions in the context of the restrictions imposed during the Delhi protests. A challenge was raised to the constitutional validity of Section 163, BNSS. Section 163 BNSS replaced Section 144 of the erstwhile Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC). It empowers designated magistrates to issue urgent orders to prevent danger to human life, public safety, disturbances of public tranquillity or other specified threats. Such orders can restrict assemblies, processions and other activities. The Court, however, said it would not go into the validity of Section 163 BNSS, since it had earlier already upheld the corresponding provision in the CrPC (Section 144). " Oral submissions were made with regard to the vires of Section 163 BNSS. However, as the pari materia provision of Section 144 CrPC has been upheld in Babulal Parate v. State of Maharashtra, (1961) 3 SCR 423, we are not inclined to entertain the same, " the Court said. items.title: FDI, fundraising and filings: Practical answers to questions every founder, CFO and in-house counsel should be asking
items.summary: In this Leading Questions piece, Sheena Ogra and Avantika Shukla address some of the key questions surrounding corporate compliances and FEMA compliance that organisations need to keep in mind in the context of fundraising and foreign investment. As India's startup and investment ecosystem continues to evolve, regulatory compliance has become far more than a post-closing formality. Any non-compliance in maintaining secretarial records or failure to undertake necessary filings with regulatory authorities can not only expose an organisation to hefty penalties but, where the organisation is looking to raise funds, can also invariably affect investor confidence, thereby causing delays in closing a transaction and, in certain instances, even affect the overall goodwill of such an organisation. Therefore, in this piece, we address the legal and practical considerations that a company should keep in mind from a compliance standpoint to minimise potential risks and strengthen its focus on being compliant before, during and after a fundraise or equity infusion. Question: What board and shareholder approvals should a company obtain before accepting foreign direct investment (FDI)? Answer: The first step is to check whether the proposed investment falls under the automatic route or requires prior government approval under the FDI policy and other applicable laws in India. This assessment should include evaluation of the sectoral cap, pricing requirements, investor eligibility and any sector-specific conditions. Once that is clear, the company should obtain the necessary corporate approvals. Typically, the Board approves the proposed fundraising and its key terms, authorises the execution of the transaction documents, approves the issue and allotment of securities, and takes such other actions as may be required to implement and complete the transaction. If the investment is through a preferential issue, shareholders' approval by way of a special resolution is also required, along with necessary filings with the Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act, 2013 (“Companies Act”). Companies should also ensure they comply with FEMA pricing guidelines, obtain the necessary valuation report and, where applicable, complete the dematerialisation of their securities, as these aspects should not be left for the end of the transaction. items.title: Senior counsel Gopal Sankaranarayanan withdraws from Delhi protest cases before Supreme Court
items.summary: Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan has withdrawn from seven matters concerning the Delhi protests before the Supreme Court following repeated interruptions and the alleged snatching of his microphone during Thursday's hearing. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi on Thursday heard around 46 petitions concerning alleged police brutality, unlawful detentions, restrictions on public movement, journalists' rights and the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. When Bar & Bench reached out to Sankaranarayanan to confirm his decision to withdraw from the cases, the senior counsel said, "The bench failed to control the court. I cannot continue like this. Dignity of the court is more important." Sankaranarayanan expressed concern over the lack of order during the hearing, particularly the manner in which matters were taken up without following their serial numbers. He added that preserving the dignity and decorum of the Court was more important than continuing his appearances in the cases. CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi Sources told the Bar & Bench that Sankaranarayanan, who was briefed in the seven matters, has communicated to his clients that he would no longer appear in the proceedings. The sources added that Sankaranarayanan had attended the hearing fully prepared with his notes and briefs. However, he was repeatedly interrupted by other counsel while attempting to address the bench. As a result, he was unable to complete his submissions. Towards the end of the proceedings, when he sought to make further submissions, a senior woman lawyer appearing on the same side allegedly snatched the microphone from him. Sankaranarayanan subsequently walked out of the courtroom before the proceedings concluded. His withdrawal from the matter assumes significance given his involvement in multiple petitions raising questions about Delhi Police action, detentions and restrictions on the right to protest. The Court on Thursday issued notices to Central government and Delhi Police in several petitions and directed law enforcement agencies to preserve CCTV footage and other digital evidence. The bench also appointed nodal counsel for both sides and directed them to segregate the overlapping petitions into broad categories by October 28, enabling separate counter-affidavits. The main protest-related batch is listed for hearing on November 3.

items.title: Supreme Court asks Sanjay Raut to explain conduct over remarks against judiciary
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked Shiv Sena (UBT) Member of Parliament (MP) Sanjay Raut to explain his remarks criticising the Chief Justice of India (CJI) for refusing to meet Opposition leaders. A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi passed the order while hearing a petition filed by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders challenging the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the functioning of the Election Commission of India (ECI). Raut is also a petitioner in the case. The Court said it was allowing him to participate in the proceedings only on a provisional basis till he explains his conduct. "In W.P. (C) No. 1351/2026 (Item 25), the petition on behalf of Petitioner No. 6 is entertained on a provisional basis, subject to his explaining his conduct,” the bench said. CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi Raut had criticised the CJI's refusal to meet Gandhi and other Opposition leaders over issues concerning the functioning of the ECI. He had claimed that 80 Supreme Court and High Court judges were seen playing badminton with political leaders in London. “You can meet them, play with them, have dinner or lunch with them, with Chief Ministers. You can suddenly resign to join a political party. You don’t care for principles and law then but when we want to meet you to save democracy…you say we will not meet political leaders,” Raut had said. In another interaction with the media, Raut had said that judges freely attend political programs of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and that its Chief Ministers organize dinners to welcome them. Pertinently, Attorney General R Venkataramani has granted consent for initiating criminal contempt proceedings against Raut and journalist Nikhil Wagle over their remarks concerning the CJI and the judiciary. The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA), which had sought the Attorney General's consent to initiate contempt proceedings, clarified in its petition that photographs presented as being from a badminton event in London were actually from an event held at Thyagaraj Stadium in New Delhi in November 2025.
